# Story 15 — CRM Completion, AI Features & Platform Administration (Story: 15)

## Prerequisites

- Stories 3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 24 completed and merged on `main` (per intake §7).
- Coordinate with owners of `AdminController`, `TicketsController`, `OutboundWebhookDispatcher`, `AppShell.tsx`, and `PortalShell.tsx` — this story touches many long-lived surfaces.
- Because of the scope size, execute the phases below **in order** (each is a hard checkpoint). Do not batch them.

---

## Story Goal

Bring the CRM to its originally-agreed target state by shipping, in one coordinated feature:

1. Full Admin-driven staff user CRUD + role assign/revoke UI on top of the existing `AdminController.AssignRole` mechanism.
2. A global, filterable Admin-only Audit Log viewer.
3. `TicketTask` due/lead-time reminders and Agent-to-Agent `@mentions` on ticket notes, both flowing through the existing `Notification`/`NotificationBell` pipeline.
4. HMAC-signed outbound webhook delivery on top of the existing `OutboundWebhookDispatcher`.
5. A provider-agnostic **AI abstraction** (mirroring `IChannelSender`) plus five capabilities wired through it: ticket summary, suggested reply, suggested category/priority, suggested KB articles, and a distinct AI chatbot. A `NotConfigured` degradation mode analogous to `EmailSender`/`WhatsappSender`/`SmsSender` is a **required deliverable**.
6. Platform administration: runtime-editable **SLA targets** (replacing the hardcoded `TicketsController.SlaTargets`) and runtime **reminder lead-time** (§4.3), plus **Department**, **Branch**, and **Branding** (name/logo/theme) settings surfaced in `AppShell.tsx` and `PortalShell.tsx`.

**Explicitly not in scope:** any real paid AI/Email/WhatsApp/SMS vendor account; ERP; customer-level notes/attachments; KB content-type distinctions; granular per-permission RBAC beyond the existing role model; rewriting the Story 14/24 branch collision in git history; any change to Stories 1–13 or Story 24's existing behaviour.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** `SlaTargets` is a hardcoded dictionary in `TicketsController`; reminder lead time does not exist; no user creation UI; audit log has only per-ticket / per-customer scoped views; outbound webhooks are signed with nothing; no AI code anywhere; no Department/Branch; no branding.
- **New behaviour:** all of the above are Admin-editable at runtime through a new `RuntimeSettings` + `Branding` mechanism, all AI capabilities flow through one provider-agnostic interface, outbound webhooks carry an HMAC signature header, and the notification pipeline additionally emits reminder + mention notifications.
- **Silent auto-application is forbidden** for AI category/priority — the agent's manual choice always wins. AI output is a *suggestion*, never a mutation.
- **No general chat/presence/team-messaging** is to be built. `@mention` on a note is the sole and complete "collaboration" surface.
- **Backward compatibility** with Stories 1–13 and Story 24: every change is additive; existing endpoints/pages keep their shapes.

### Phase 5 — Task reminders + Agent @mentions

**Testability split (required):** do not put the scan logic directly inside a
`BackgroundService.ExecuteAsync` - that method isn't callable the way this codebase's
existing test harness works (every test in `CustomerSupportCrm.Api.Tests` calls a plain
method directly; there is no hosted-service test fixture in this project and none should
be introduced for this alone). Instead:

Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/BackgroundServices/ITaskReminderScanner.cs`
```csharp
public interface ITaskReminderScanner
{
    // Runs one scan; returns the number of reminders created. Directly callable from a
    // test with an injected AppDbContext - no hosting required.
    Task<int> ScanAndNotifyAsync(DateTime nowUtc, CancellationToken ct);
}
```
Implement `TaskReminderScanner : ITaskReminderScanner` (scoped service, takes `AppDbContext` +
`IRuntimeSettings` via constructor - this is a plain application service, not a
per-action controller, so constructor injection is the correct convention here, same as
`AuditLogger`/`JwtTokenService`):
- Read `RuntimeSettingKeys.ReminderLeadHrs`.
- For each `TicketTask` where `Done == false` and `DueAtUtc != null` and
  `DueAtUtc <= nowUtc + leadHours` and no prior reminder exists for that task
  (`Notifications.Any(n => n.SourceTaskId == task.Id && n.Type == "TaskReminder")`),
  create a `Notification { Type = "TaskReminder", SourceTaskId = task.Id, UserId = task owner }`.

Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/BackgroundServices/TaskReminderBackgroundService.cs`
- A thin `BackgroundService` wrapper: on a timer (5 min default, a constant is
  acceptable - not itself a runtime setting), create a DI scope and call
  `ITaskReminderScanner.ScanAndNotifyAsync(DateTime.UtcNow, ct)`. No business logic lives
  here - it exists only to give the scanner a periodic trigger in the running app.

File: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Domain/Notification.cs`
- **Do not introduce a new C# enum.** This codebase discriminates every such field with a plain validated string (`Ticket.Status`/`Category`/`Priority`/`Source`, `ChannelMessage.Direction`, etc.) - never a C# enum - and `Notification.Type` already exists as exactly this kind of string field (`"Assigned"`/`"Escalated"` today). Extend its allow-list with two new values, `"TaskReminder"` and `"Mention"`, instead of adding a parallel `Kind` enum alongside it.
- Add `Guid? SourceTaskId`, `Guid? SourceTicketNoteId` (both nullable, mirroring how `TicketId` on this same entity is already "kept nullable for future non-ticket types").
- **Invariant (comment on the entity, next to these two properties):** exactly one of
  `SourceTaskId`/`SourceTicketNoteId` is non-null when `Type` is `"TaskReminder"` /
  `"Mention"` respectively; both are null for every other `Type` (`"Assigned"`,
  `"Escalated"`). Never populate both on the same row. This is a construction-time
  discipline documented at each of the two call sites below (Phase 5's scanner and the
  note-mention action already only ever set their own one field) - consistent with how
  this codebase enforces every other string-discriminator invariant (by convention and
  code review, not a DB `CHECK` constraint or a private-constructor/factory redesign,
  since no other entity here uses either of those patterns).
- **No FK relationship on either field - bare `Guid?`, no `HasOne`/`HasForeignKey`, no
  navigation property.** This mirrors the established "generic reference id, no FK"
  precedent already used by `AuditLog.ActorUserId` and
  `OutboundWebhookSubscription.CreatedByUserId` in this exact codebase, and is not
  optional here: `TicketsController.DeleteTask` (Story 9, already shipped) deletes a
  `TicketTask` row independently of its ticket. If `SourceTaskId` were a real FK to
  `TicketTask.Id`, deleting a task that has ever had a reminder fired for it would throw a
  foreign-key constraint violation, breaking an existing, already-working feature. A bare
  id avoids this entirely - a notification's source becoming stale/orphaned after its
  task or note is gone is acceptable (matches how `AuditLog.Details` already tolerates
  referencing since-deleted rows elsewhere in this codebase).

File: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Data/AppDbContext.cs` (`Notification` config)
- Add a **filtered unique index** enforcing "exactly once" for task reminders at the
  database level, not only via the application-level `Any(...)` guard in
  `ITaskReminderScanner` (which is correct for this project's current single-instance
  deployment, but a DB constraint is strictly more robust against any future concurrent
  scan/restart scenario, at zero extra cost): `e.HasIndex(n => n.SourceTaskId).IsUnique().HasFilter("[Type] = 'TaskReminder' AND [SourceTaskId] IS NOT NULL")`.
  This mirrors the exact filtered-unique-index pattern this codebase already established
  for `Customer.Email`/`Customer.Phone` - a value that must be unique only among the rows
  where it's actually meaningful. Include this index in the same migration that adds the
  `SourceTaskId`/`SourceTicketNoteId` columns.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Deactivated user with an active JWT** — token remains valid until expiry. Trigger: rejection at `AuthController` login only. Document the residual window in `AuthController.cs`; do not add token revocation (out of scope of the RBAC-only mandate).
- **Empty/absent `RuntimeSetting`** — `IRuntimeSettings.GetAsync<T>` returns `default`. Every consumer (`TicketsController`'s SLA lookup, `ITaskReminderScanner`, `BrandingController`) must supply a hardcoded fallback that matches today's behaviour. Enforced in each call site.
- **Duplicate task reminders** — trigger: background service runs while a prior reminder exists, or two scans overlap. Primary guard: the `Notifications.Any(n => n.SourceTaskId == task.Id && n.Type == "TaskReminder")` check in `ITaskReminderScanner`. Backstop: the filtered unique index on `Notification.SourceTaskId` (Phase 5) makes a genuine duplicate insert fail at the database level even if the application-level check ever races - catch and swallow that specific constraint violation in the scanner (it means another concurrent scan already created the reminder, which is the desired outcome, not an error).
- **Mentioning a deactivated user** — reject with `400` at note-create; the picker in `TicketDetailPage.tsx` must filter `IsActive == false`.
- **Mentioning yourself** — allowed; do not produce a notification for the actor (matches assignment behavior). Enforced in the note-create action.
- **Outbound webhook with `SigningSecret == null`** — should never happen after the migration back-fills existing rows; if it does, dispatcher logs a warning and sends without the header (do **not** drop the delivery — preserves failure-isolation contract). Enforced in `OutboundWebhookDispatcher`.
- **AI provider = `NullAiProvider`** — every controller action returns `200 OK` with `status: "NotConfigured"`. The frontend must never render a red error state for this case; must always render the neutral "AI unavailable" banner.
- **AI provider timeout / exception** — wrap the provider call in `try/catch` inside `AiController`, translate to `AiStatus.ProviderError`. The underlying ticket workflow is untouched.
- **Branding logo too large** — DTO validator rejects `> 256 KB`. Enforced in `BrandingController`.
- **RTL / Arabic** — every new page uses logical Tailwind classes (`ps-`, `pe-`, `start-`, `end-`). No `pl-`/`pr-`/`left-`/`right-`.
- **Concurrent runtime-setting write** — `RuntimeSettings.SetAsync` uses a last-writer-wins update on `Key`; log the previous value into `AuditLog`.
- **Migration partially applied** — `AddPlatformAdminFoundations` is additive only (new tables + nullable columns); rollback = `dotnet ef database update <previous>`; no data loss.
- **Story 24 (`PublicApiController` / `WebhookSubscriptionsController`)** unchanged in shape; only `OutboundWebhookDispatcher` and the `OutboundWebhookSubscription` entity gain a nullable field.

## Test Plan

**Harness reality check (binding on every item below):** every test in
`backend/tests/CustomerSupportCrm.Api.Tests` calls a controller action, or a plain
service method, directly as C# - the same pattern as `ChannelsControllerInboundTests.cs`,
`ReportsControllerTests.cs`, and Story 24's `ApiKeysControllerTests.cs`. This harness
**never** runs the ASP.NET Core request pipeline, so it cannot execute authentication
middleware or `[Authorize]` policy evaluation - it cannot prove a live 401/403. Where an
item below would need that, it is a **metadata-only** check (confirms the
`[Authorize(...)]` attribute is present and correct, same pattern as
`ReportsController_HasAdminOnlyAuthorizationAttribute` / Story 24's
`ApiKeysController_HasAdminOnlyAuthorizationAttribute`) and the live 401/403 outcome is
listed under Manual/Runtime Verification, not claimed here.

**Also binding:** `frontend/package.json` has no test runner configured anywhere in this
project (confirmed across every prior story) and none is introduced by this plan -
adding one (Vitest/Jest/Testing Library) would be new infrastructure this plan does not
authorize. Every frontend behavior below is therefore verified manually, not by a
`*.test.tsx` file.

### Automated tests (existing unit/controller-direct-call style — no new test dependency)

Backend (`backend/tests/CustomerSupportCrm.Api.Tests/`):

1. **`AdminUsersControllerTests.cs`** (new) — direct action calls: create user persists
   correctly and hashes the initial password; list returns expected shape; deactivate
   sets `IsActive = false`; reactivate sets it back to `true`; role add/revoke delegates
   to the existing `AssignRole`/removal internals correctly. Plus
   **`AdminController_HasAdminOnlyAuthorizationAttribute`** - metadata-only, confirms
   `[Authorize(Policy = "RequireStaff", Roles = "Admin")]` is present on the controller.
   Does **not** prove a live 403 for a non-Admin or 401 for anonymous - see Manual/Runtime
   Verification.
2. **`AuthControllerDeactivatedUserTests.cs`** (new) — direct call: a login attempt for a
   `User` with `IsActive == false` is rejected by the login action's own logic, with the
   same stable error code as invalid credentials (no account-existence leak). This tests
   the login action's internal branch directly - it does not prove the HTTP-level
   behavior end-to-end, which is Manual/Runtime Verification.
3. **`AdminAuditLogFilterTests.cs`** (new) — direct call: action/actor/date-range filters
   and paging return the expected subset of seeded `AuditLog` rows.
4. **`RuntimeSettingsTests.cs`** (new) — `IRuntimeSettings.SetAsync` then `GetAsync` round-trips
   a value; cache is invalidated on `SetAsync`; `GetAsync` returns `default` when the key
   is absent.
5. **`TicketsControllerSlaRuntimeTests.cs`** (new) — direct calls, not an HTTP round-trip:
   call `IRuntimeSettings.SetAsync(RuntimeSettingKeys.SlaTargets, ...)` directly, then call
   `TicketsController.Create` directly and assert the new due dates reflect the just-set
   values; call `Create` again with no setting present and assert the existing hardcoded
   defaults are used unchanged.
6. **`TaskReminderScannerTests.cs`** (new) — direct calls to
   `ITaskReminderScanner.ScanAndNotifyAsync`: a reminder fires for a task within the
   configured lead window and sets `Type == "TaskReminder"` + `SourceTaskId` (and leaves
   `SourceTicketNoteId` null); a second scan does not duplicate it; a task with
   `Done == true` is skipped. Also assert the created row never has both `SourceTaskId`
   and `SourceTicketNoteId` set. (This is exactly why Phase 5 splits the scanner out of
   the `BackgroundService` - the scanner is a plain injectable service this harness can
   call directly; the `BackgroundService` wrapper itself is not unit-tested, only its
   scanner.)
7. **`TicketNoteMentionTests.cs`** (new) — direct call to the note-create action: a
   mention creates a `Notification` with `Type == "Mention"` + `SourceTicketNoteId` set
   (and `SourceTaskId` left null); an unknown mentioned user id → `400`; a deactivated
   mentioned user id → `400`; mentioning oneself creates no notification.
8. **`OutboundWebhookSigningTests.cs`** (new) — direct call to
   `OutboundWebhookDispatcher.DispatchAsync` against a captured `HttpClient`: the
   `X-Squad-Signature`/`X-Squad-Timestamp` headers are present and the signature verifies
   against the stored secret and body; a tampered body fails verification.
9. **`AiControllerNullProviderTests.cs`** (new) — direct calls to `AiController`'s five
   actions with `NullAiProvider` injected: every action returns `status: "NotConfigured"`,
   and calling the underlying ticket-workflow actions (create/reply/categorize) directly
   afterwards still succeeds unaffected. This is the primary evidence for the
   credential-independent Acceptance Criteria.
10. **`AiControllerMockProviderTests.cs`** (new) — direct calls with `MockAiProvider`
    injected: every action returns `status: "Ok"` with the mock's canned values. This is
    the primary evidence for the credential-dependent Acceptance Criteria - it requires no
    real vendor account.
11. **`DepartmentsBranchesControllerTests.cs`** (new) — direct calls: CRUD logic for both
    entities; a `User`/`Ticket` can be assigned a `DepartmentId`/`BranchId`.
12. **`BrandingControllerTests.cs`** (new) — direct calls: `GET` returns the stored
    branding or a sensible default when unset; `PUT` persists via `IRuntimeSettings`; a
    logo payload over 256 KB is rejected with `400`.
13. Update the existing `OutboundWebhookDispatcher`-adjacent assertions in
    `ChannelsControllerOutboundTests.cs` (Story 12) if they inspect the outbound request
    shape, so they still pass once the new headers are added - this is a regression check,
    not new coverage.

### Manual/Runtime verification (requires the real HTTP pipeline or a running browser — this project has no integration-test harness, and none is introduced by this plan)

- 403 for a non-Admin staff JWT on every new `/api/admin/*`, `/api/departments`,
  `/api/branches`, and `PUT /api/branding` route; 401 for anonymous on the same routes
  (except `GET /api/branding`, which is deliberately anonymous - confirm it succeeds with
  no token).
- A deactivated user's existing JWT is rejected specifically at the next **login**
  attempt (the documented residual-window caveat: an already-issued, still-valid token is
  not proactively revoked).
- The `@mention` autocomplete in `TicketDetailPage.tsx` only offers active staff users,
  and the mentioned agent sees the notification in `NotificationBell.tsx`, visually
  distinguishable from an assignment notification.
- The AI buttons in `TicketDetailPage.tsx`/`TicketsPage.tsx` render the neutral
  "unavailable" banner with `NullAiProvider` configured, and render real (mock) content
  with `MockAiProvider` configured, without ever blocking the underlying manual ticket
  workflow.
- The AI chatbot widget is reachable as a distinct entry point from the existing human
  Live Chat widget.
- An Admin can edit the SLA targets and the reminder lead time from their respective
  pages and see each take effect without a deploy.
- An Admin can edit branding (name/logo/color) and see both `AppShell.tsx` and
  `PortalShell.tsx` reflect it.
- Full i18n parity: diff `en.json`/`ar.json` key sets (the same script-based check used
  in every prior story) - no automated CI gate exists for this in the current project and
  none is introduced here.
- RTL sweep: switch to Arabic and click through every new page (Users, Audit Log, SLA
  Targets, Reminder Lead Time, Branding, Departments, Branches) - no layout breaks.
- Full regression pass: log in as staff and as a portal customer and confirm every Story
  1-13 and Story 24 flow named in Verification Step 6 below still works.

## Migration / Rollback

- Single EF migration `AddPlatformAdminFoundations` covering: `User.IsActive`, `User.DepartmentId`, `User.BranchId`, `Ticket.DepartmentId`, `Ticket.BranchId`, `Departments`, `Branches`, `RuntimeSettings`, `Notification.SourceTaskId`/`SourceTicketNoteId` + the filtered unique index on `SourceTaskId` (no change to `Notification.Type`'s column definition - only new allowed string values; no FK added on either new column), `OutboundWebhookSubscription.SigningSecret`. All new columns nullable or defaulted; strictly additive.
- Data back-fill: within the migration, `UPDATE OutboundWebhookSubscriptions SET SigningSecret = <generated>` for existing rows so Phase 4's verification works everywhere.
- Rollback: `dotnet ef database update <previous>` — safe because no existing column is dropped or narrowed.
- Half-applied risk: if the migration ran but Phase 6 (AI) code is not deployed, all AI endpoints simply 404 — no user impact. If the app runs against a pre-migration DB, `IRuntimeSettings` will throw at first read — deploy order **must** be migration first, then app.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** `dotnet build backend/CustomerSupportCrm.sln`
2. **Backend automated tests:** `dotnet test backend/CustomerSupportCrm.sln` — proves the
   direct-call logic items in the Test Plan's Automated Tests section (entity/CRUD logic,
   the reminder scanner, mention validation, webhook signing, both AI providers, RBAC
   *metadata* presence). Does **not** prove any live 401/403 — that is step 9.
3. **Migration applies:** `dotnet ef database update --project backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api`
4. **Frontend builds/type-checks:** `npm run build` in `frontend/` (match whatever the
   repo currently uses; do not switch package manager or introduce a test runner).
5. **Frontend runs:** `npm run dev` in `frontend/`.
6. **Regression — Stories 1–13 & 24 (manual):** smoke each area listed in intake §7:
   - Story 3 login still works.
   - Story 4 role check on an existing protected endpoint still 403s for a non-Admin.
   - Story 5 per-ticket audit history still renders unchanged.
   - Story 9 tasks, notes, quick replies untouched.
   - Story 10 assignment notification still fires with `Type == "Assigned"` (unchanged).
   - Story 11 KB portal unchanged.
   - Story 12 channels, `ChatHub`, `ChatWidget` unchanged (AI chatbot is distinct).
   - Story 24 public API + webhooks continue to work; delivery now carries the `X-Squad-Signature` header.
7. **Credential-independent AI check (manual):** with `AiOptions.Provider` empty, exercise
   each AI button — each must show the "AI unavailable / not configured" state; ticket
   workflows must be unaffected.
8. **Credential-dependent AI check (manual):** set `AiOptions.Provider = "mock"`, re-run
   the same flows; each must return real (canned) values. **Document** in the PR that this
   was verified via `MockAiProvider` and that a real-vendor pass is deferred.
9. **Manual/runtime pipeline verification (not covered by step 2):** 403/401 on every new
   admin route for a non-Admin/anonymous caller respectively (except the deliberately
   anonymous `GET /api/branding`); a deactivated user's next login attempt is rejected;
   the mention notification is visible and distinguishable in `NotificationBell.tsx`.
10. **RTL sweep:** switch language to `ar` and click through Users, Audit Log, SLA
    Targets, Reminder Lead Time, Branding, Departments, Branches — no layout breaks.
11. **i18n parity:** diff `en.json`/`ar.json` key sets (same script-based check as every
    prior story).

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `User.IsActive` added; deactivated users cannot log in; historical rows intact.
- [ ] Admin can create/list/edit/deactivate staff users through `UsersPage.tsx` without touching DB or seed script.
- [ ] Admin can add and revoke a role assignment through `UsersPage.tsx`, reusing `AdminController.AssignRole` internals.
- [ ] `AuditLogPage.tsx` renders the global log with action / actor / date-range filters.
- [ ] Reminder lead time is stored in `RuntimeSettings`; `ITaskReminderScanner` (invoked periodically by the thin `TaskReminderBackgroundService` wrapper) produces exactly one `Notification` per task within the window; visible in `NotificationBell`.
- [ ] `@mention` on a ticket note creates a `Notification` with `Type == "Mention"`, distinguishable from `"Assigned"` in `NotificationBell`; no chat/presence surface added.
- [ ] Every outbound webhook carries `X-Squad-Signature: sha256=…` and `X-Squad-Timestamp`; altered payload fails verification (test in `OutboundWebhookSigningTests.cs`).
- [ ] `IAiProvider` exists with `NullAiProvider` and `MockAiProvider`; no controller/page hardcodes a vendor SDK.
- [ ] With `NullAiProvider` active, all five AI capabilities return `status: NotConfigured` and the frontend renders the neutral banner; ticket create/reply/categorize/KB-browse unaffected.
- [ ] With `MockAiProvider` active, ticket summary, suggested reply (insertable into a note), suggested category/priority (never silently applied), suggested KB articles, and the AI chatbot all return real values through the abstraction.
- [ ] `TicketsController.SlaTargets` hardcoded dictionary removed; SLA target hours edited in `SlaTargetsPage.tsx` are reflected in new tickets without a code deploy.
- [ ] `Department` and `Branch` entities + admin CRUD; a `User` (and a `Ticket`) can be assigned to both.
- [ ] Branding (name, logo, primary colour) editable in `BrandingPage.tsx`; `AppShell.tsx` and `PortalShell.tsx` reflect it via `useBranding()` instead of the hardcoded app name.
- [ ] All new UI strings present in both `en.json` and `ar.json`; RTL sweep passes.
- [ ] Full existing backend test suite green; existing Story 1–13 and Story 24 flows manually smoke-checked and unchanged.
- [ ] PR documents which credential-dependent AI criteria were verified via `MockAiProvider` and which (if any) remain untested pending a real provider account.
